bio.en: Architectural designer currently based in Tokyo, working across architecture, interiors, visualization, and emerging design technologies. Drawn to projects that connect culture, memory, and public life, while constantly exploring how digital tools can reshape the way spaces are imagined and produced.
bio.ja: 東京を拠点に、公共建築や商業複合施設の設計、ビジュアライゼーション、そして新たなデザインテクノロジーの領域を横断して活動する建築デザイナー。文化、記憶、公共空間の関係性に関心を持ちながら、テクノロジーを通して空間と人との関係をどのように再構築できるかを探求している。
bio.zh: 现居东京的建筑设计师，工作涵盖公共建筑、商业综合体、可视化以及新兴设计科技领域。对于文化、记忆与公共空间之间的联系，同时乐于探索如何运用科技重新塑造空间与人的关系。

en.cardDescription: A public museum shaped through the spatial memory of the local dragon kiln, pairing ceramic material research with a quieter civic presence.
en.detailIntro: Inspired by the local dragon kiln, the museum reinterprets Yixing’s clay culture through form, materiality, and public space.
en.detailBody1: The project translates the heritage of purple clay and ceramic craft into a contemporary museum environment, connecting local material culture with a new public destination.
en.detailBody2: Facade texture, roof geometry, and spatial sequence were developed through close studies of local kilns, ceramic samples, and construction logic.
en.metaRole: Architecture, interior, landscape, furniture & signage; DD drawings

en.cardDescription: A competition proposal exploring how neighborhood life can be rebuilt through shared proximity, care, and everyday encounters.
en.detailIntro: A proposal for a former elementary school site in Meguro, rethinking civic space through shared programs and local relationships.
en.detailBody1: The project imagines proximity as an architectural and social framework, where everyday activities can become a softer form of urban infrastructure.

en.cardTitle: If Eaves Dropped: Rethinking Privacy NOW
en.cardDescription: A thesis project exploring transient privacy through curvilinear spaces, partial enclosure, and shared domestic life.
en.detailTitle: If Eaves Dropped: Rethinking Privacy NOW
en.detailIntro: The project redefines privacy as something separated from ownership, formed through gradients of enclosure and moments of temporary retreat.
en.detailBody1: Curvilinear spaces and columns create conditions that connect and separate without fully enclosing, allowing privacy to emerge as a shifting spatial experience.
en.metaRole: Thesis project, in collaboration with Mia Shucong Wang

role.ja: 設計スタジオ・リサーチプロジェクト

en.cardDescription: A speculative addition to Shinjuku Station exploring line, infrastructure, and the relationship between humans and machines.
en.detailIntro: Set within Shinjuku Station, the project investigates how exposed systems and infrastructural lines can produce a new civic experience.
en.detailBody1: By foregrounding ducts, cords, circulation, and machine systems, the project turns everyday transit into an encounter with the hidden mechanics of the city.

en.cardDescription: A terraced museum in a historic longtang neighborhood, framing the tension between old fabric and new cultural life.
en.detailIntro: Located at the center of a renovated historic neighborhood, the museum acts as a node linking old and new, history and culture.
en.detailBody1: The terraced form offers changing views of Zhangyuan, while the sunken entrance connects the museum to underground transit, commercial programs, and public space.
en.metaRole: Concept massing, SD materials, consultant coordination

en.cardDescription: A retail concept shaped around brand atmosphere, threshold, and the choreography of entering from the street.
en.detailIntro: A concept store proposal exploring how a compact retail space can create a stronger sense of arrival and brand immersion.
en.detailBody1: The design works through thresholds, material atmosphere, and visual control to distinguish the store from its surrounding commercial environment.

en.cardTitle: Porosity: Tama Art University Library Analysis
en.cardDescription: An architectural analysis of porosity through arches, apertures, view cones, and layered modes of representation.
en.detailTitle: Porosity: Tama Art University Library Analysis
en.detailIntro: This research project studies Toyo Ito’s Tama Art University Library through the idea of porosity.
en.detailBody1: The analysis moves from geometric arches to framed viewpoints and material representation, drawing from architectural drawings and animation techniques.

en.cardTitle: Wuxi Concert Hall and Commercial Complex
en.cardDescription: A cultural complex where concert hall, museum, commerce, and landscape form a network of public event spaces.
en.detailTitle: Wuxi Concert Hall and Commercial Complex
en.detailIntro: Inspired by the vineyard typology, the project treats the site itself as an extended concert hall for music and public life.
en.detailBody1: Semi-circular forms become eaves, terraces, staircases, and plazas, creating a connected landscape for cultural events, exhibitions, and everyday gathering.
en.metaRole: Urban planning concept, concert hall design, visualization

en.cardTitle: Fluid yet Defined: Columbia University Baker Athletic Complex
en.cardDescription: A boathouse proposal using arches to organize movement, visibility, and shared athletic life along the water.
en.detailTitle: Fluid yet Defined: Columbia University Baker Athletic Complex
en.detailIntro: The project explores fluidity and definition through a structural system of connected arches.
en.detailBody1: Different circulation paths for athletes, students, and visitors are organized through porous spatial boundaries, encouraging interaction while maintaining clarity.
en.metaRole: Design studio project, in collaboration with Jingfei Huang
